subject: Banking
title: The Advisory Business
description: A quick, practical guide to The Advisory Business.

hook.text: When Disney bought 21st Century Fox for $71.3 billion, investment bankers from Goldman Sachs advised both sides.

buildup.text: Advisory fees on mega-deals range from 0.1% to 1% of deal value. On $71 billion, even 0.2% is $142 million in fees.

discovery.text: Banks advise on valuation, negotiation strategy, deal structure, and regulatory approval. They quarterback the process.

twist.text: Conflicts arise when the same bank advises buyer and seller.

climax.text: Advisory is the purest investment banking service. No capital at risk, just expertise sold at enormous hourly rates.

punchline.text: $142 million for advice on one deal. Expertise at scale.

quiz.question: What do investment bank advisors do in a merger?
options: Advise on valuation, strategy, and deal structure for fees

details.summary: The advisory business is the core of investment banking, where bankers counsel companies on mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, and restructurings, earning percentage-based fees on completed transactions that can reach tens of millions.
details.whyItMatters: Advisory work influences which companies merge, which get sold, and how industries consolidate. The advice of a handful of banks shapes the structure of the global economy through billions in deals completed annually.
takeaways: Advisory fees are typically 0.5 to 2 percent of the deal's transaction value
Both the buyer and seller in a merger hire separate advisory banks
Top advisory roles are called managing directors and carry immense influence

faq.question: How much do investment banks charge for M&A advice?
faq.answer: Fees range from 0.5 to 2 percent of deal value, with smaller deals commanding higher percentages. A 10 billion dollar merger might generate 50 to 100 million in advisory fees split between the buyer's and seller's banks.

faq.question: Do companies really need investment bank advisors?
faq.answer: For large deals, yes. Banks provide valuation expertise, buyer or seller identification, negotiation leverage, and credibility with boards and shareholders. The advisory fee is small relative to the value at stake in billion-dollar transactions.
